title: Gračanica Monastery
description: King Stefan Milutin builds the church that is among the finest of late Byzantine architecture.

title: Visoki Dečani founded
description: King Stefan Dečanski begins the largest medieval church in the Balkans, where he is buried.

title: Second Battle of Kosovo
description: Murad II defeats the Hungarian army of John Hunyadi, ending the last attempt to drive the Ottomans from the Balkans.

title: Ottomans take Novo Brdo
description: Mehmed II captures the richest silver-mining town of the Balkans, and Kosovo passes under Ottoman rule.

title: Patriarchate of Peć restored
description: With the support of the vizier Sokollu Mehmed Pasha the Serbian patriarchate is re-established at Peć.

title: Kosovo Vilayet created
description: The Ottoman government forms a province of Kosovo, much larger than today's country.

title: Albanian revolt of 1910
description: Albanians rise against the taxes and conscription of the Young Turk government and are put down by a large army.

title: Serbia takes Kosovo
description: In the First Balkan War the Serbian army occupies Kosovo, ending more than four centuries of Ottoman rule.

title: Kosovo joined to Italian Albania
description: After the Axis defeat of Yugoslavia most of Kosovo is attached to Albania, then under Italy.

title: Bujan Conference
description: Communist delegates from Kosovo call for union with Albania after the war, a resolution the Yugoslav party sets aside.

title: Protests of 1968
description: Albanian students demand a republic of Kosovo, the first such open demand in socialist Yugoslavia.

title: Autonomy under the 1974 constitution
description: The new Yugoslav constitution gives Kosovo its own assembly, government and seat in the federal presidency, almost the standing of a republic.

title: Protests of 1981
description: Student protests over conditions at the university grow into demands for a republic and are put down by the army.

title: Trepča miners' strike
description: Albanian miners stay underground on hunger strike against the removal of Kosovo's autonomy, which Serbia carries through the next month.

title: Republic of Kosova declared
description: Albanian members of the dissolved assembly declare Kosovo a republic and build parallel schools and clinics.

title: Rugova elected president
description: In elections Serbia does not recognise, Ibrahim Rugova, leader of the non-violent resistance, is chosen president.

title: Attack on Prekaz
description: Serbian police kill the guerrilla leader Adem Jashari and more than fifty of his family, and the Kosovo Liberation Army grows into a mass movement.

title: Račak massacre
description: The killing of 45 Albanians by Serbian forces turns Western governments towards intervention.

title: Rambouillet talks
description: Talks on self-government under a NATO force fail when Yugoslavia refuses to sign.

title: Security Council Resolution 1244
description: After 78 days of NATO bombing, the Security Council places Kosovo under United Nations administration.

title: NATO troops enter Kosovo
description: The Kosovo Force moves in as Yugoslav forces withdraw, and most of the refugees return within weeks.

title: Unrest of March 2004
description: Riots against Serbs leave 19 people dead and dozens of churches and monasteries burned or damaged.

title: Ahtisaari Plan
description: The United Nations envoy Martti Ahtisaari proposes independence under international supervision, which Serbia and Russia reject.

title: Declaration of independence
description: The assembly of Kosovo declares independence from Serbia, which most Western states recognise and Serbia does not.

title: Opinion of the International Court of Justice
description: The court finds that the declaration of independence did not break international law.

title: Brussels Agreement
description: Kosovo and Serbia agree, with the European Union as mediator, on steps to normalise their relations.
